title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
abstract: arXiv:2610.39302v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Whether models trained on different modalities converge to the same representation of the world is central to AI. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) conjectures that they do as they scale, but without a proof it offers neither a guarantee nor a recipe. We turn the hypothesis into a theorem. First, we prove a \emph{Platonic Representation Theorem}: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) trained separately on any number of modalities learn the same representation up to one rotation whenever their positive pairs are two observations of one scene--\emph{good views}--and their misalignment is bounded otherwise. Second, we show that next-token prediction is a JEPA with \emph{bad views}, parts of a single document, which explains why language models align with vision only through scale. Third, we validate the theory from 145k captions to the texts of 940M web images, and uncover a scaling law of alignment that predicts unsee

translated_title: 用JEPA（联合嵌入预测架构）证明并改进柏拉图表征假说
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.39302v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：在不同模态上训练的模型是否会收敛到对世界的同一种表征，这是人工智能领域的核心问题。柏拉图表征假说（PRH）推测随着规模的扩大它们会趋于一致，但由于缺乏证明，该假说既无法提供保证，也无法给出实现方法。我们将这一假说变成了一个定理。首先，我们证明了一个“柏拉图表征定理”：联合嵌入预测架构（JEPA）无论在多少种模态上分别训练，只要其正样本对是同一场景的两次观测——即“好视角”——就会学习到仅相差一次旋转的相同表征；否则，其错位程度是有界的。其次，我们证明下一个词预测本质上就是一种使用“坏视角”（即单个文档的各个部分）的JEPA，这解释了为什么语言模型只有通过规模才能与视觉对齐。第三，我们从14.5万条字幕到9.4亿张网络图像的文本对该理论进行了验证，并揭示出一个对齐缩放定律，可以预测未见（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 本文首次将柏拉图表征假说证明为定理，表明只要正样本对是同一场景的“好视角”，在不同模态上分别训练的JEPA必然收敛到仅差一次旋转的相同世界表征，并据此解释了语言模型因使用“坏视角”而只能依靠规模才能与视觉对齐，同时通过大规模实验发现了可预测对齐效果的新缩放定律。
en_tdlr: This paper turns the Platonic Representation Hypothesis into a theorem, proving that JEPAs trained separately on any modalities converge to the same representation up to a rotation when their positive pairs are "good views" of one scene, explains why next-token prediction (a JEPA with "bad views") aligns with vision only through scale, and validates a new scaling law of alignment from 145k captions to 940M web images.
